- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially after sharp drops.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >65), model frequently overcorrects with steep upward trend; cap forecast growth to avoid overshoot.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d drop from 70+ to 55+), model often fails to recognize it; add downward bias or lagged momentum correction.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast curve or reduce sensitivity to sentiment swings.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30d moving average of history, adjust forecast to align with recent mean rather than extrapolation.
- If sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model often underperforms; add conservative downward adjustment or trigger “low sentiment” correction rule.
